subject: obstetrics-gynaecology
title: Abruptio Placentae: Concealed Haemorrhage and Couvelaire Uterus

steps.tx: Premature separation of a normally sited placenta before delivery is **abruptio placentae**. It causes painful bleeding, a tense tender uterus and fetal distress or death. Hypertension and trauma are leading associations. It complicates about one percent of pregnancies, and half the perinatal deaths come from the prematurity that follows.
steps.say: Abruptio placentae separates the placenta early, causing painful bleeding and fetal distress.

steps.tx: Bleeding trapped behind the placenta with little or nothing visible outside is **concealed haemorrhage**. Shock seems out of proportion to visible loss because litres hide behind the placenta. The uterus feels woody hard and larger than dates. Blood loss of one to two litres can hide there, so the fundal height is marked and measured serially.
steps.say: Concealed haemorrhage hides litres behind the placenta with shock out of proportion.

steps.tx: Blood dissecting into the uterine muscle and under the serosa, seen at caesarean, is the **Couvelaire uterus**. The purple bruised uterus usually still contracts after delivery. It is not by itself an indication for hysterectomy. Hysterectomy is needed only when the uterus will not contract or bleeding cannot be controlled otherwise.
steps.say: Couvelaire uterus bruises the muscle purple with blood but usually still contracts.

steps.tx: Fetal outcome depends on separation extent, with complete separation causing **intrauterine death**. The retroplacental clot interrupts all exchange. Live fetuses need immediate delivery, usually caesarean, alongside maternal resuscitation. Kleihauer testing in Rh negative women sizes the fetomaternal bleed that often accompanies abruption.
steps.say: Complete separation causes intrauterine death, and live fetuses need immediate delivery.

steps.tx: Abruption consumes clotting factors and triggers disseminated coagulation, so **coagulation screening** is urgent. Fibrinogen falls earliest and predicts severity. Blood products including fibrinogen concentrate restore haemostasis. Fibrinogen under 2 grams per litre in abruption predicts severe postpartum haemorrhage and guides concentrate dosing.
steps.say: Coagulation screening in abruption tracks fibrinogen, which falls earliest and predicts severity.

steps.tx: A tender, irritable uterus contracting almost continuously is described as **uterine hypertonus**. The baseline tone stays high between contractions, starving the fetus. Tocodynamometry shows this pattern clearly. The tracing shows a high resting tone with frequent small contractions and a fetal heart that recovers poorly.
steps.say: Uterine hypertonus keeps baseline tone high and starves the fetus between contractions.

steps.tx: Cocaine use, smoking, hypertension and abdominal trauma head the list of **abruption risk factors**. Previous abruption recurs in about one in ten next pregnancies. Pre-eclampsia management reduces but does not abolish the risk. Recurrence after one abruption is about 10 percent, rising toward 25 percent after two.
steps.say: Abruption risk factors include hypertension, trauma, smoking and previous abruption.

steps.tx: When the fetus is dead and mother stable, vaginal delivery avoids surgery through a coagulopathic field, following **vaginal preference**. Amniotomy and oxytocin expedite labour. Coagulopathy is corrected in parallel with blood products. Artificial rupture helps by releasing pressure and letting the uterus contract down on the bleeding area.
steps.say: Vaginal preference avoids surgery through a coagulopathic field when the fetus is dead.

steps.tx: After abruption delivery, atonic bleeding threatens because blood soaked muscle contracts poorly, termed **postpartum atony risk**. Active third stage management and uterotonics are mandatory. Fibrinogen is rechecked in recovery. Tranexamic acid within three hours of birth adds protection when atony follows an abruption.
steps.say: Postpartum atony risk follows abruption because blood soaked muscle contracts poorly.
